svg.title: CH-PU schematic

text.tspan: CH-PU: pickup dynamic input · schematic (PROPOSED, Phase 2)
Fixed HV-rated top divider, switched low-voltage bottom leg, 1.65 V bias, buffered into the Pico ADC. Pickup comparators give edge timing. Default after reset = ±100 V range.
VTHP = V_BIAS + x, VTHN = V_BIAS − x (x set by firmware,
typically 5–25 % of full scale). Window 1.25–2.05 V.
U3 footprint: dual comparator, SOIC-8, standard pinout
(TLV3202 or MCP6542; pull-ups DNP for push-pull parts).

svg.text: 6 · Optional peak hold (footprints, DNP until needed)

text.tspan: Catches narrow pulses that the sampled waveform could miss.
D4 / D5 = BAT54 (Schottky). The diode drop (about 0.25 V) is
calibrated out by the self-test. Reset: drive the 1 kΩ reset line
low (PK+) or high (PK−) for 1 ms, then back to high-Z.
• Ranges: S1 → R_B5 (±5 V), S2 → R_B20 (±20 V), S3 → R_B100 (±100 V). Node swing ±1.5 V = full scale. Only one switch on at a time.
• R_T1 + R_T2 = 200 kΩ: two 0.6 W metal-film resistors in series (about 350 V each), so a wrong 400 V connection only draws about 2 mA.
• Self-test: with the clips open, PU_TEST drives 3.3 V / 0 V through R_INJ. Expected output steps: 0.56 V (±5 V), 0.12 V (±20 V), 23 mV (±100 V).
• 3V3A = 3V3 through 10 Ω, 10 µF and 100 nF. IC supply pins have 100 nF each. Pickup frequency range: DC to about 20 kHz.
⚠ Pickup coils only. Never connect IN+ / IN− to a CDI output or an ignition coil.
A pickup can reach tens of volts at speed. The TVS, R_T1/R_T2 and the clamp protect against that, not against a CDI output
(200–400 V pulses) or HT. Keep the pickup disconnected from the CDI while testing. See docs/safety.md.
The clamp diodes sit on a plug-in header so they can be replaced without desoldering.
